statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genomic time trees place a buildup of lineage-splitting events both before and shortly after the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
statements.evidence: Genomic time trees reveal an accumulation of cladogenic events before and immediately after the Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) boundary
statements.note: The abstract reports that genomic time trees show cladogenic events accumulating before and immediately after the K-Pg boundary.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The conflicts between X-chromosome and autosome phylogenies in Cenozoic clades were caused by incomplete lineage sorting rather than hybridization.
statements.evidence: Conversely, X-chromosome versus autosome conflicts characterize multiple independent clades that radiated during the Cenozoic.
statements.note: The abstract says where X-versus-autosome conflicts occur but names no cause for them, neither incomplete lineage sorting nor hybridization.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across an alignment of 241 placental genomes, relationships among mammalian orders showed relatively low phylogenomic conflict, whatever dataset or analytical method was used.
statements.evidence: Interordinal relationships exhibit relatively low rates of phylogenomic conflict across diverse datasets and analytical methods.
statements.note: The abstract states that interordinal relationships show relatively low rates of phylogenomic conflict across diverse datasets and analytical methods.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In several independent clades that radiated during the Cenozoic, the X chromosome and the autosomes give conflicting phylogenetic signals.
statements.evidence: X-chromosome versus autosome conflicts characterize multiple independent clades that radiated during the Cenozoic
statements.note: The abstract reports that X-chromosome versus autosome conflicts characterize multiple independent clades that radiated in the Cenozoic.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Biogeographical modelling forecasts that populations of many bread wheat relatives will keep shrinking over the coming decades because of their vulnerability to climate change.
statements.evidence: Further biogeographical modelling predicted a continued population shrinking of many bread wheat relatives in the coming decades because of their vulnerability to the changing climate.
statements.note: The abstract reports that biogeographical modelling predicts continued population shrinking of many bread wheat relatives in the coming decades owing to climate vulnerability.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Over roughly the last 2,000 years, the cultivated relatives of bread wheat saw their populations decrease by about 82%, attributed to a shift in human food choice.
statements.evidence: the cultivated relatives of bread wheat experienced a population decline by ~82% over the past ~2,000 yr due to the food choice shift of humans
statements.note: The abstract states that the cultivated relatives of bread wheat declined by about 82% over the past ~2,000 years because of a shift in human food choice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole-genome data from 795 accessions place the origin of bread wheat on the southwest Caspian coast, with speciation drawn out over about 3,300 years by persistent gene flow.
statements.evidence: we found that bread wheat originated from the southwest coast of the Caspian Sea and underwent a slow speciation process, lasting ~3,300 yr owing to persistent gene flow from its relatives
statements.note: The abstract reports an origin on the southwest coast of the Caspian Sea and a slow speciation lasting about 3,300 years because of persistent gene flow from relatives.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Convergent adaptation of bread wheat in Europe and East Asia involved selection on the same flowering-time genes.
statements.evidence: Soon after, bread wheat spread across Eurasia and reached Europe, South Asia and East Asia ~7,000 to ~5,000 yr ago, shaping a diversified but occasionally convergent adaptive landscape in novel environments.
statements.note: The abstract mentions an occasionally convergent adaptive landscape but names no genes or traits under selection, so flowering-time genes are neither stated nor ruled out.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: AMY1 and AMY2A each went through repeated duplication and deletion events at rates up to over 10,000 times the SNP mutation rate, whereas AMY2B duplications arose just once.
statements.evidence: AMY1 and AMY2A genes each underwent multiple duplication/deletion events with mutation rates up to more than 10,000-fold the single-nucleotide polymorphism mutation rate, whereas AMY2B gene duplications share a single origin.
statements.note: The abstract reports mutation rates up to more than 10,000-fold the SNP rate for AMY1 and AMY2A duplication/deletion events and a single origin for AMY2B duplications.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Agricultural populations carry higher amylase gene copy numbers than populations that live by fishing, hunting or pastoralism.
statements.evidence: We find that amylase genes have higher copy numbers in agricultural populations than in fishing, hunting and pastoral populations.
statements.note: The abstract states that amylase genes have higher copy numbers in agricultural populations than in fishing, hunting and pastoral populations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Nearly identical amylase structures recurred on different haplotype backgrounds because of non-allelic homologous recombination between flanking repeats.
statements.evidence: We identify 28 distinct amylase structural architectures and demonstrate that nearly identical structures have arisen recurrently on different haplotype backgrounds throughout recent human history.
statements.note: The abstract reports that nearly identical structures arose recurrently on different haplotypes but does not name the mutational mechanism behind them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ancient genomes show that amylase haplotypes carrying duplications rose rapidly in frequency in West Eurasians over the past 12,000 years, consistent with positive selection.
statements.evidence: Leveraging 533 ancient human genomes, we find that duplication-containing haplotypes (with more gene copies than the ancestral haplotype) have rapidly increased in frequency over the past 12,000 years in West Eurasians, suggestive of positive selection.
statements.note: Using 533 ancient genomes, the abstract reports a rapid rise of duplication-containing haplotypes over the past 12,000 years in West Eurasians, suggestive of positive selection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The phylogenetic cross-bracing approach yielded a highly resolved, dated species tree and an absolute timeline for the evolution of ATP synthase.
statements.evidence: This approach results in a highly resolved, dated species tree and establishes an absolute timeline for ATP synthase evolution.
statements.note: The abstract states that the cross-bracing approach produced a highly resolved, dated species tree and an absolute timeline for ATP synthase evolution.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Of the two ATP synthase lineages, the F-type is the ancestral form from which the A/V-type form derived.
statements.evidence: Our analyses show that the divergence of ATP synthase into F- and A/V-type lineages was a very early event in cellular evolution dating back to more than 4 Ga
statements.note: The abstract dates the split into F- and A/V-type lineages but does not say which of the two forms is ancestral to the other.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Eukaryotic nuclear (2.67-2.19 Ga) and mitochondrial (2.58-2.12 Ga) lineages split from their nearest prokaryotic relatives at about the same time, with a slightly longer nuclear stem-lineage.
statements.evidence: the eukaryotic nuclear and mitochondrial lineages diverged from their closest archaeal (2.67-2.19 Ga) and bacterial (2.58-2.12 Ga) relatives at approximately the same time, with a slightly longer nuclear stem-lineage
statements.note: The abstract dates the nuclear-archaeal split to 2.67-2.19 Ga and the mitochondrial-bacterial split to 2.58-2.12 Ga, roughly contemporaneous, with a slightly longer nuclear stem-lineage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The split of ATP synthase into F-type and A/V-type lineages happened very early in cellular evolution, over 4 billion years ago.
statements.evidence: the divergence of ATP synthase into F- and A/V-type lineages was a very early event in cellular evolution dating back to more than 4 Ga
statements.note: The abstract dates the divergence of ATP synthase into F- and A/V-type lineages to more than 4 Ga, a very early event in cellular evolution.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The reconstructed ancestral population sizes were larger for ape ancestors than for the ancestors of Old World monkeys.
statements.evidence: We exploit ILS to reconstruct speciation times and ancestral population sizes.
statements.note: The abstract says ancestral population sizes were reconstructed but reports no values and no comparison between ape and monkey ancestors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At individual ancestral nodes of the primate tree, incomplete lineage sorting affected as much as 64% of the genome.
statements.evidence: We find up to 64% of the genome affected by ILS at individual nodes.
statements.note: The abstract reports that up to 64% of the genome is affected by ILS at individual nodes of the primate phylogeny.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Incomplete lineage sorting is found in excess among immune-function genes but in deficit among housekeeping genes.
statements.evidence: we show an excess of ILS in genes with immune functions and a deficit of ILS in housekeeping genes
statements.note: The abstract reports an excess of ILS in genes with immune functions and a deficit of ILS in housekeeping genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Speciation times estimated from incomplete lineage sorting fall much later than genomic divergence times and agree well with the fossil record.
statements.evidence: Estimated speciation times are much more recent than genomic divergence times and are in good agreement with the fossil record.
statements.note: The abstract states that estimated speciation times are much more recent than genomic divergence times and agree well with the fossil record.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In all three sexes, the main quantitative trait loci for hybrid sterility were located on the fused chromosome ChrIR.
statements.evidence: Quantitative trait locus analyses for hybrid sterility in all three sexes revealed that major quantitative trait loci mapped to the fused chromosome ChrIR.
statements.note: The abstract reports that QTL analyses for hybrid sterility in all three sexes mapped the major loci to the fused chromosome ChrIR.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genomic and cytogenetic analyses that included an outgroup species point to two separate fusion events, both involving chromosome ChrIR, between P. pacificus and P. exspectatus.
statements.evidence: Strikingly, genomic characterization and cytogenetic studies including outgroup species Pristionchus occultus indicated two independent fusions involving the same chromosome, ChrIR, between these related species.
statements.note: The abstract states that genomic and cytogenetic studies including the outgroup P. occultus indicated two independent fusions involving ChrIR between the two species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Chromosome fusions likewise drive hybrid sterility between closely related Caenorhabditis species.
statements.evidence: Thus, recent chromosome fusions repatterned recombination rate and drove reproductive isolation during Pristionchus speciation.
statements.note: The study examines only Pristionchus species and says nothing about chromosome fusions or hybrid sterility in Caenorhabditis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The fusions reshaped the chromosome-wide recombination pattern, producing large regions in which recombination is reduced.
statements.evidence: Genetic linkage analysis indicated that these fusions altered the chromosome-wide pattern of recombination, resulting in large low-recombination regions
statements.note: The abstract reports that linkage analysis showed the fusions altered the chromosome-wide recombination pattern and created large low-recombination regions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Orchids trace back to a common ancestor that lived in Laurasia during the Late Cretaceous.
statements.evidence: The orchids' most recent common ancestor is inferred to have lived in Late Cretaceous Laurasia.
statements.note: The abstract infers that the most recent common ancestor of orchids lived in Late Cretaceous Laurasia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Speciation rates were highest in Panama and Costa Rica, and the bulk of modern orchid species diversity arose within the last 5 million years.
statements.evidence: Despite their ancient origin, modern orchid species diversity mainly originated over the last 5 Ma, with the highest speciation rates in Panama and Costa Rica.
statements.note: The abstract states that modern orchid species diversity mainly originated over the last 5 Ma, with the highest speciation rates in Panama and Costa Rica.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Explosive orchid speciation in Central America was driven mainly by shifts between different pollinator groups.
statements.evidence: These results alter our understanding of the geographic origin of orchids, previously proposed as Australian, and pinpoint Central America as a region of recent, explosive speciation.
statements.note: The abstract identifies Central America as a region of recent, explosive speciation but gives no cause for it, pollinator-related or otherwise.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The present-day range of Apostasioideae, two genera with 16 species spanning India to northern Australia, is interpreted as a relict distribution.
statements.evidence: The modern range of Apostasioideae, which comprises two genera with 16 species from India to northern Australia, is interpreted as relictual
statements.note: The abstract interprets the modern range of Apostasioideae, two genera with 16 species from India to northern Australia, as relictual.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Roughly 80% of the deleterious mutations affecting neutral diversity lie outside exons, and phylogenetic conservation is the best predictor of regions under purifying selection.
statements.evidence: The regions under purifying selection are best predicted by phylogenetic conservation, with ~80% of the deleterious mutations affecting neutral diversity occurring in non-exonic regions.
statements.note: The abstract states that phylogenetic conservation best predicts regions under purifying selection and that ~80% of the relevant deleterious mutations are non-exonic.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Background selection is also the main form of linked selection shaping genetic diversity on the human X chromosome.
statements.evidence: We address this question in humans by fitting a model of the joint effects of selective sweeps and background selection to autosomal polymorphism data from the 1000 Genomes Project.
statements.note: The model was fitted only to autosomal polymorphism data, so the abstract says nothing about linked selection on the X chromosome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with background selection, selective sweeps had a smaller effect on linked neutral diversity in humans.
statements.evidence: when both modes of selection are considered jointly, selective sweeps are estimated to have had little or no effect on linked neutral diversity
statements.note: Fitted jointly, selective sweeps are estimated to have had little or no effect on linked neutral diversity, while background selection is the dominant mode of linked selection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Once variation in mutation rate is controlled for, background selection by itself accounts for about 60% of the variance in megabase-scale diversity.
statements.evidence: After controlling for variation in mutation rates along the genome, a model of background selection alone explains ~60% of the variance in diversity levels at the megabase scale.
statements.note: The abstract reports that, after controlling for mutation-rate variation, a model of background selection alone explains ~60% of the variance in megabase-scale diversity.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mosquito lineages that shifted to feeding on mammals diversified faster than lineages that kept feeding on other hosts.
statements.evidence: mosquito diversification and host-use patterns within major lineages appear to coincide in earth history both with major continental drift events and with the diversification of vertebrate classes
statements.note: The abstract links diversification and host use to events in earth history but does not compare diversification rates between mammal-feeding and other lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analysing 709 single-copy ortholog groups from 256 species yielded a strongly supported mosquito phylogeny that resolves the major vector species and lineages.
statements.evidence: we used phylogenomic analysis of 709 single copy ortholog groups from 256 mosquito species to produce a strongly supported phylogeny that resolves the position of the major disease vector species and the major mosquito lineages
statements.note: The abstract reports a strongly supported phylogeny from 709 single-copy ortholog groups in 256 species that resolves the major vector species and mosquito lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study dates the origin of mosquitoes to about 217 million years ago in the early Triassic, considerably older than previous estimates.
statements.evidence: Our analyses support an origin of mosquitoes in the early Triassic (217 MYA [highest posterior density region: 188-250 MYA]), considerably older than previous estimates.
statements.note: The abstract places the origin of mosquitoes in the early Triassic at 217 MYA (188-250 MYA), considerably older than previous estimates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Host-association data show that mosquitoes switched to feeding on mammalian blood on many separate occasions.
statements.evidence: mosquitoes have shifted to feeding upon the blood of mammals numerous times
statements.note: The abstract reports, from a database of host associations, that mosquitoes have shifted to feeding on mammalian blood numerous times.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: All five ARGs show signs of recent horizontal gene transfer within or across Listeria species, according to phylogenetic and recombination analyses.
statements.evidence: phylogenetic and recombination analyses provide evidence of recent horizontal gene transfer (HGT) in all five ARGs within and/or across species
statements.note: The abstract reports phylogenetic and recombination evidence of recent HGT in all five ARGs within and/or across species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 594 genomes of soil Listeria, the lincomycin resistance gene lin was the commonest of five putatively functional ARGs, followed by mprF, sul, fosX and norB.
statements.evidence: Among the five putatively functional ARGs identified, lin, which confers resistance to lincomycin, is the most prevalent, followed by mprF, sul, fosX, and norB.
statements.note: The abstract ranks lin as the most prevalent of the five putatively functional ARGs, ahead of mprF, sul, fosX and norB.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Antibiotic resistance genes occur mainly in Listeria sensu stricto species, and species closer to L. monocytogenes tend to carry more ARGs.
statements.evidence: ARGs are predominantly found in Listeria sensu stricto species, with those more closely related to L. monocytogenes tending to harbor more ARGs.
statements.note: The abstract states that ARGs are found predominantly in Listeria sensu stricto and that species more closely related to L. monocytogenes tend to harbor more ARGs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: L. monocytogenes isolates from human listeriosis cases carry the same five ARGs at frequencies similar to those in soil isolates.
statements.evidence: Here, we characterize ARGs in 594 genomes representing 19 Listeria species that we previously isolated from soils in natural environments across the United States.
statements.note: The study analysed only isolates from natural soils, so the abstract says nothing about ARGs in clinical listeriosis isolates.
